labels.note: A pattern line: each `$:` line plays at the same time as the others.

labels.label: S$:
labels.note: Solo: when one or more lines start with `S$:`, only those lines play.
Mute: a line whose label starts (or ends) with `_` does not play.

functions.name: accelerate
functions.description: A pattern of numbers that speed up (or slow down) samples while they play. Currently only supported by osc / superdirt.

functions.name: add
functions.description: Assumes a pattern of numbers. Adds the given number to each item in the pattern.

functions.name: addVoicings
functions.description: Adds a new custom voicing dictionary.

params.name: dictionary
params.description: maps chord symbol to possible voicings

functions.name: adsr
functions.description: ADSR envelope: Combination of Attack, Decay, Sustain, and Release.

functions.name: aliasBank
functions.description:
Register an alias for a bank of sounds.
Optionally accepts a single argument map of bank aliases.
Optionally accepts a single argument string of a path to a JSON file containing bank aliases.

params.name: alias
params.description: - The alias to use for the bank

functions.name: almostAlways
functions.description: Shorthand for `.sometimesBy(0.9, fn)`

functions.name: almostNever
functions.description: Shorthand for `.sometimesBy(0.1, fn)`

functions.name: always
functions.description: Shorthand for `.sometimesBy(1, fn)` (always calls fn)

functions.name: amp
functions.description: Like `gain`, but linear.

functions.name: anchor
functions.description: The top note to align the voicing to. Defaults to c5

params.name: anchorNote
params.description: the note to align the voicings to

functions.name: appBoth
functions.description:
When this method is called on a pattern of functions, it matches its haps
with those in the given pattern of values.  A new pattern is returned, with
each matching value applied to the corresponding function.

In this `_appBoth` variant, where timespans of the function and value haps
are not the same but do intersect, the resulting hap has a timespan of the
intersection. This applies to both the part and the whole timespan.

functions.name: appLeft
functions.description:
As with `appBoth`, but the `whole` timespan is not the intersection,
but the timespan from the function of patterns that this method is called
on. In practice, this means that the pattern structure, including onsets,
are preserved from the pattern of functions (often referred to as the left
hand or inner pattern).

functions.name: appRight
functions.description:
As with `appLeft`, but `whole` timespans are instead taken from the
pattern of values, i.e. structure is preserved from the right hand/outer
pattern.

functions.name: appWhole
functions.description:
Assumes 'this' is a pattern of functions, and given a function to
resolve wholes, applies a given pattern of values to that
pattern of functions.

functions.name: arp
functions.description: Selects indices in in stacked notes.

functions.name: arpWith
functions.description: Selects indices in in stacked notes.

functions.name: arrange
functions.description:
Allows to arrange multiple patterns together over multiple cycles.
Takes a variable number of arrays with two elements specifying the number of cycles and the pattern to use.

functions.name: as
functions.description: Sets properties in a batch.

params.name: mapping
params.description: the control names that are set

functions.name: asym
functions.description: Asymmetrical diode distortion

functions.name: attack
functions.description: Amplitude envelope attack time: Specifies how long it takes for the sound to reach its peak value, relative to the onset.

functions.name: bank
functions.description: Select the sound bank to use. To be used together with `s`. The bank name (+ "_") will be prepended to the value of `s`.
examples: s("bd sd [~ bd] sd").bank('RolandTR909') // = s("RolandTR909_bd RolandTR909_sd")

functions.name: beat
functions.description:
creates a structure pattern from divisions of a cycle
especially useful for creating rhythms

functions.name: begin
functions.description: A pattern of numbers from 0 to 1. Skips the beginning of each sample, e.g. `0.25` to cut off the first quarter from each sample.

params.name: amount
params.description: between 0 and 1, where 1 is the length of the sample

functions.name: berlin
functions.description:
Generates a continuous pattern of [berlin noise](conceived by Jame Coyne and Jade Rowland as a joke but turned out to be surprisingly cool and useful,
like perlin noise but with sawtooth waves), in the range 0..1.

functions.name: binary
functions.description: Creates a binary pattern from a number.

params.name: n
params.description: - input number to convert to binary

functions.name: binaryL
functions.description: Creates a binary list pattern from a number.

params.name: n
params.description: - input number to convert to binary s("saw").seg(8) .partials(binaryL(irand(4096).add(1)))

functions.name: binaryN
functions.description: Creates a binary pattern from a number, padded to n bits long.

params.name: n
params.description: - input number to convert to binary

functions.name: binaryNL
functions.description: Creates a binary list pattern from a number, padded to n bits long.

params.name: n
params.description: - input number to convert to binary

functions.name: bite
functions.description:
Splits a pattern into the given number of slices, and plays them according to a pattern of slice numbers.
Similar to `slice`, but slices up patterns rather than sound samples.

functions.name: bmod
functions.description:
Modulates with the output from a given `bus`.
Can be called in sequence like pat.bmod(...).bmod(...) to set up multiple modulators

Send to an audio bus with `otherPat.bus(..)`.

There are two ways to declare which control will be modulated:
1. Explicitly put `control` in the config (e.g. `bmod({ id: 2, c: "lpf" })`)
2. If the control parameter is absent, the control _immediately before_ the `bmod` call will be used
  (e.g. `s("saw").lpf(500).bmod({ id: 2 })` to modulate `lpf`)

Modulators can be referred to by `id` so that they can be updated later e.g. inside
a `sometimes`. See example below.

params.name: config.bus
params.description: Bus to get modulation signal from

params.name: config.subControl
params.description: Sub-control name to append to the control key. Aliases: sc

params.name: config.depth
params.description: Relative modulation depth. Aliases: dep, dr

params.name: id
params.description: ID to use for this modulator

functions.name: bpattack
functions.description: Sets the attack duration for the bandpass filter envelope.

params.name: attack
params.description: time of the bandpass filter envelope

functions.name: bpdc
functions.description: DC offset of the LFO for the bandpass filter

params.name: dcoffset
params.description: dc offset. set to 0 for unipolar

functions.name: bpdecay
functions.description: Sets the decay duration for the bandpass filter envelope.

params.name: decay
params.description: time of the bandpass filter envelope

functions.name: bpdepth
functions.description: Depth of the LFO for the bandpass filter

functions.name: bpdepthfrequency
functions.description: Depth of the LFO for the bandpass filter, in HZ

functions.name: bpenv
functions.description: Sets the bandpass filter envelope modulation depth.

params.name: modulation
params.description: depth of the bandpass filter envelope between 0 and _n_

functions.name: bpf
functions.description:
Sets the center frequency of the **b**and-**p**ass **f**ilter. When using mininotation, you
can also optionally supply the 'bpq' parameter separated by ':'.

functions.name: bpq
functions.description: Sets the **b**and-**p**ass **q**-factor (resonance).

functions.name: bprate
functions.description: Rate of the LFO for the bandpass filter

functions.name: bprelease
functions.description: Sets the release time for the bandpass filter envelope.

params.name: release
params.description: time of the bandpass filter envelope

functions.name: bpshape
functions.description: Shape of the LFO for the bandpass filter

functions.name: bpskew
functions.description: Skew of the LFO for the bandpass filter

params.name: skew
params.description: How much to bend the LFO shape

functions.name: bpsustain
functions.description: Sets the sustain amplitude for the bandpass filter envelope.

params.name: sustain
params.description: amplitude of the bandpass filter envelope

functions.name: bpsync
functions.description: Cycle-synced rate of the LFO for the bandpass filter

functions.name: brak
functions.description:
Returns a new pattern where every other cycle is played once, twice as
fast, and offset in time by one quarter of a cycle. Creates a kind of
breakbeat feel.

functions.name: brand
functions.description: A continuous pattern of 0 or 1 (binary random)

functions.name: brandBy
functions.description: A continuous pattern of 0 or 1 (binary random), with a probability for the value being 1

functions.name: bus
functions.description:
A `bus` is a send which can be used for mixing patterns. It combines with..
  s("bus") to play that bus through another pattern (for, say, applying non-linear
  effects like distortion to multiple signals)

  otherPat.bmod(..) (to modulate another pattern with the bus)

functions.name: busgain
functions.description: Postgain multiplier prior to sending the signal to the audio bus.

functions.name: byteBeatExpression
functions.description: Create byte beats with custom expressions

functions.name: byteBeatStartTime
functions.description: Create byte beats with custom expressions

functions.name: ccn
functions.description: MIDI control number: Sends a MIDI control change message.

functions.name: ccv
functions.description: MIDI control value: Sends a MIDI control change message.

functions.name: ceil
functions.description:
Assumes a numerical pattern. Returns a new pattern with all values set to
their mathematical ceiling. E.g. `3.2` replaced with `4`, and `-4.2`
replaced with `-4`.

functions.name: channel
functions.description: Choose the channel the pattern is sent to in superdirt

functions.name: channels
functions.description: Allows you to set the output channels on the interface

functions.name: chebyshev
functions.description: Distortion via Chebyshev polynomials

functions.name: choose
functions.description: Chooses randomly from the given list of elements.

functions.name: choose2
functions.description:
As with choose, but the pattern that this method is called on should be
in the range -1 .. 1

functions.name: chooseCycles
functions.description: Picks one of the elements at random each cycle.

functions.name: chooseInWith
functions.description:
As with {chooseWith}, but the structure comes from the chosen values, rather
than the pattern you're using to choose with.

functions.name: chooseWith
functions.description:
Choose from the list of values (or patterns of values) using the given
pattern of numbers, which should be in the range of 0..1

functions.name: chop
functions.description:
Cuts each sample into the given number of parts, allowing you to explore a technique known as 'granular synthesis'.
It turns a pattern of samples into a pattern of parts of samples.
examples:
samples({ rhodes: 'https://cdn.freesound.org/previews/132/132051_316502-lq.mp3' })
s("rhodes")
 .chop(4)
 .rev() // reverse order of chops
 .loopAt(2) // fit sample into 2 cycles

functions.name: chord
functions.description: The chord to voice

params.name: symbols
params.description: chord symbols to voice e.g., C, Eb, Fm7, G7. The symbols can be defined via addVoicings

examples: chord("<Am C D F Am E Am E>").voicing()

functions.name: chorus
functions.description: mix control for the chorus effect

functions.name: chunk
functions.description: Divides a pattern into a given number of parts, then cycles through those parts in turn, applying the given function to each part in turn (one part per cycle).

functions.name: chunkBack
functions.description: Like `chunk`, but cycles through the parts in reverse order. Known as chunk' in tidalcycles

functions.name: chunkBackInto
functions.description: Like `chunkInto`, but moves backwards through the chunks.
examples:
sound("bd sd ht lt bd - cp lt").chunkInto(4, hurry(2))
  .bank("tr909")

functions.name: chunkInto
functions.description: Like `chunk`, but the function is applied to a looped subcycle of the source pattern.
examples:
sound("bd sd ht lt bd - cp lt").chunkInto(4, hurry(2))
  .bank("tr909")

functions.name: clip
functions.description: Multiplies the duration with the given number. Also cuts samples off at the end if they exceed the duration.

functions.name: coarse
functions.description: Fake-resampling for lowering the sample rate. Caution: This effect seems to only work in chromium based browsers

params.name: factor
params.description: 1 for original 2 for half, 3 for a third and so on.

functions.name: color
functions.description: Sets the color of the hap in visualizations like pianoroll or highlighting.

functions.name: compress
functions.description: Compress each cycle into the given timespan, leaving a gap
examples:
cat(
  s("bd sd").compress(.25,.75),
  s("~ bd sd ~")
)

functions.name: compressor
functions.description:
Dynamics Compressor. The params are `compressor("threshold:ratio:knee:attack:release")`
More info [here](https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/API/DynamicsCompressorNode?retiredLocale=de#instance_properties)

functions.name: contract
functions.description:
*Experimental*

Contracts the step size of the pattern by the given factor. See also `expand`.

functions.name: control
functions.description: MIDI control: Sends a MIDI control change message.

functions.name: cosine
functions.description: A cosine signal between 0 and 1.

functions.name: cosine2
functions.description: A cosine signal between -1 and 1 (like `cosine`, but bipolar).

functions.name: crush
functions.description: Bit crusher effect.

params.name: depth
params.description: between 1 (for drastic reduction in bit-depth) to 16 (for barely no reduction).

functions.name: cubic
functions.description: Cubic polynomial distortion

functions.name: cut
functions.description: In the style of classic drum-machines, `cut` will stop a playing sample as soon as another samples with in same cutgroup is to be played. An example would be an open hi-hat followed by a closed one, essentially muting the open.

functions.name: cyclesPer
functions.description:
A pattern measuring the duration of events,
in cycles per event. `cyclesPer` doesn't have structure itself, but takes structure, and therefore
event durations, from the pattern that it is combined with.
For example `cyclesPer.struct("1 1 [1 1] 1")` would give the same as `"0.25 0.25 [0.125 0.125] 0.25"`.
See also its reciprocal, `per`, also known as `perCycle`.
examples:
sound("bd sd [bd bd] sd*4 [- sd] [bd [bd bd]]")
  .note(cyclesPer.add(20))

functions.name: decay
functions.description:
Amplitude envelope decay time: the time it takes after the attack time to reach the sustain level.
Note that the decay is only audible if the sustain value is lower than 1.

functions.name: defaultmidimap
functions.description: configures the default midimap, which is used when no "midimap" port is set

functions.name: defragmentHaps
functions.description:
Combines adjacent haps with the same value and whole.  Only
intended for use in tests.

functions.name: degrade
functions.description: Randomly removes 50% of events from the pattern. Shorthand for `.degradeBy(0.5)`

functions.name: degradeBy
functions.description:
Randomly removes events from the pattern by a given amount.
0 = 0% chance of removal
1 = 100% chance of removal

functions.name: delay
functions.description:
Sets the level of the delay signal.

When using mininotation, you can also optionally add the 'delaytime' and 'delayfeedback' parameter,
separated by ':'.

functions.name: delayfeedback
functions.description:
Sets the level of the signal that is fed back into the delay.
Caution: Values >= 1 will result in a signal that gets louder and louder! Don't do it

functions.name: delayspeed
functions.description: Sets the time of the delay effect.

params.name: delayspeed
params.description: controls the pitch of the delay feedback

functions.name: delaysync
functions.description: Sets the time of the delay effect in cycles.

functions.name: density
functions.description: Noise crackle density

functions.name: detune
functions.description: Set detune for stacked voices of supported oscillators
examples: note("d f a a# a d3").fast(2).s("supersaw").detune("<.1 .2 .5 24.1>")

functions.name: dictionary
functions.description: Which dictionary to use for the voicings. This falls back to the default dictionary if not provided

params.name: dictionaryName
params.description: which dictionary (having been defined with `addVoicings`) to use

examples:
addVoicings('house', {
'': ['7 12 16', '0 7 16', '4 7 12'],
'm': ['0 3 7']
})
chord("<Am C D F Am E Am E>")
.dict('house').anchor(66)
.voicing().room(.5)

functions.name: diode
functions.description: Diode-emulating distortion

functions.name: discreteOnly
functions.description:
Returns a new pattern, with 'continuous' haps (those without 'whole'
timespans) removed from query results.

functions.name: distort
functions.description:
Wave shaping distortion. CAUTION: it can get loud.
Second option in optional array syntax (ex: ".9:.5") applies a postgain to the output. Third option sets the waveshaping type.
Most useful values are usually between 0 and 10 (depending on source gain). If you are feeling adventurous, you can turn it up to 11 and beyond ;)

functions.name: distorttype
functions.description: Type of waveshaping distortion to apply.
examples:
s("sine").note("F1*2").release(1)
  .penv(24).pdecay(0.05)
  .distort(rand.range(1, 8))
  .distorttype("<fold chebyshev scurve diode asym sinefold>")

functions.name: distortvol
functions.description: Postgain for waveshaping distortion.

functions.name: div
functions.description: Divides each number by the given factor.

functions.name: djf
functions.description: DJ filter, below 0.5 is low pass filter, above is high pass filter.

params.name: cutoff
params.description: below 0.5 is low pass filter, above is high pass filter

functions.name: drive
functions.description: Filter overdrive for supported filter types
examples: note("{f g g c d a a#}%16".sub(17)).s("supersaw").lpenv(8).lpf(150).lpq(.8).ftype('ladder').drive("<.5 4>")

functions.name: drop
functions.description:
*Experimental*

Drops the given number of steps from a pattern.
A positive number will drop steps from the start of a pattern, and a negative number from the end.

functions.name: dry
functions.description: Set dryness of reverb. See `room` and `size` for more information about reverb.

functions.name: duckattack
functions.description:
The time required for the ducked signal(s) to return to their normal volume.

Can vary across orbits with the ':' mininotation, e.g. `duckonset("0:0.003")`.
Note: this requires first applying the effect to multiple orbits with e.g. `duckorbit("2:3")`.

functions.name: duckdepth
functions.description:
The amount of ducking applied to target orbit

Can vary across orbits with the ':' mininotation, e.g. `duckdepth("0.3:0.1")`.
Note: this requires first applying the effect to multiple orbits with e.g. `duckorbit("2:3")`.

functions.name: duckonset
functions.description:
The time required for the ducked signal(s) to reach their lowest volume.
Can be used to prevent clicking or for creative rhythmic effects.

Can vary across orbits with the ':' mininotation, e.g. `duckonset("0:0.003")`.
Note: this requires first applying the effect to multiple orbits with e.g. `duckorbit("2:3")`.
examples:
// Rhythmic
noise: s("pink").distort("2:1").orbit(4) // used rhythmically with 0.3 onset below
hhat: s("hh*16").orbit(7)
ducker: s("bd*4").bank("tr909").duckorbit("4:7").duckonset("0.3:0.003").duckattack(0.25)

functions.name: duckorbit
functions.description:
Modulate the amplitude of an orbit to create a "sidechain" like effect.

Can be applied to multiple orbits with the ':' mininotation, e.g. `duckorbit("2:3")`

functions.name: duration
functions.description: Sets the duration of the event in cycles. Similar to clip / legato, it also cuts samples off at the end if they exceed the duration.

functions.name: each
functions.description:
Applies a function to each of the running patterns separately. This is intended for future use with upcoming 'stepwise' features. See `all` for a version that applies the function to all the patterns stacked together into a single pattern.
```
$: sound("bd - cp sd")
$: sound("hh*8")
each(fast("<2 3>"))
```

functions.name: early
functions.description: Nudge a pattern to start earlier in time. Equivalent of Tidal's <~ operator

params.name: cycles
params.description: number of cycles to nudge left

functions.name: echo
functions.description: Superimpose and offset multiple times, gradually decreasing the velocity

functions.name: echoWith
functions.description: Superimpose and offset multiple times, applying the given function each time.

params.name: func
params.description: function to apply, given the pattern and the iteration index

functions.name: end
functions.description: The same as .begin, but cuts off the end off each sample.

params.name: length
params.description: 1 = whole sample, .5 = half sample, .25 = quarter sample etc..

functions.name: env
functions.description:
Configures an envelope. Can be called in sequence like pat.env(...).env(...) to set up multiple envelopes
There are two ways to declare which control will be modulated:
1. Explicitly put `control` in the config (e.g. `env({ c: "lpf" })`)
2. If the control parameter is absent, the control _immediately before_ the `env` call will be used
  (e.g. `s("saw").lpf(500).env({ a: 1 })` to modulate `lpf`)

Modulators can be referred to by `id` so that they can be updated later e.g. inside
a `sometimes`. See example below.

params.name: config.subControl
params.description: Sub-control name to append to the control key. Aliases: sc

params.name: config.depth
params.description: Relative modulation depth. Aliases: dep, dr

params.name: config.attack
params.description: Time to reach depth. Aliases: att, a

params.name: config.decay
params.description: Time to reach sustain. Aliases: dec, d

params.name: config.release
params.description: Time to return to nominal value. Aliases: rel, r

params.name: config.acurve
params.description: Snappiness of attack curve (-1 = relaxed, 1 = snappy). Aliases: ac

params.name: config.dcurve
params.description: Snappiness of decay curve (-1 = relaxed, 1 = snappy). Aliases: dc

params.name: config.rcurve
params.description: Snappiness of release curve (-1 = relaxed, 1 = snappy). Aliases: rc

params.name: id
params.description: ID to use for this modulator

examples:
s("pulse").lpf(500).env({ a: 1 })
  .env({ c: "s", a: 1 })
  .diode(0.3)
  .sometimes(x => x.env({ a: "0.5" }, 1)) // envelope #1 (0-indexed)

s("pulse").lpf(500).env({ a: 1 }, 'lpf_mod')
  .env({ c: "s", a: 1 })
  .diode(0.3)
  .sometimes(x => x.env({ a: "0.5" }, 'lpf_mod'))

functions.name: euclid
functions.description:
Changes the structure of the pattern to form an Euclidean rhythm.
Euclidean rhythms are rhythms obtained using the greatest common
divisor of two numbers.  They were described in 2004 by Godfried
Toussaint, a Canadian computer scientist.  Euclidean rhythms are
really useful for computer/algorithmic music because they can
describe a large number of rhythms with a couple of numbers.

params.name: steps
params.description: the number of steps to fill

functions.name: euclidish
functions.description:
A 'euclid' variant with an additional parameter that morphs the resulting
rhythm from 0 (no morphing) to 1 (completely 'even'). For example
`sound("bd").euclidish(3,8,0)` would be the same as
`sound("bd").euclid(3,8)`, and `sound("bd").euclidish(3,8,1)` would be the
same as `sound("bd bd bd")`. `sound("bd").euclidish(3,8,0.5)` would have a
groove somewhere between.
Inspired by the work of Malcom Braff.

params.name: steps
params.description: the number of steps to fill

params.name: groove
params.description: exists between the extremes of 0 (straight euclidian) and 1 (straight pulse)

functions.name: euclidLegato
functions.description:
Similar to `euclid`, but each pulse is held until the next pulse,
so there will be no gaps.

params.name: steps
params.description: the number of steps to fill

functions.name: euclidLegatoRot
functions.description:
Similar to `euclid`, but each pulse is held until the next pulse,
so there will be no gaps, and has an additional parameter for 'rotating'
the resulting sequence

params.name: steps
params.description: the number of steps to fill

functions.name: euclidRot
functions.description: Like `euclid`, but has an additional parameter for 'rotating' the resulting sequence.

params.name: steps
params.description: the number of steps to fill

examples:
// A Samba rhythm necklace from Brazil
note("c3").euclidRot(3,16,14)

functions.name: every
functions.description: An alias for `firstOf`

functions.name: expand
functions.description:
*Experimental*

Expands the step size of the pattern by the given factor.

functions.name: extend
functions.description:
*Experimental*

`extend` is similar to `fast` in that it increases its density, but it also increases the step count
accordingly. So `stepcat("a b".extend(2), "c d")` would be the same as `"a b a b c d"`, whereas
`stepcat("a b".fast(2), "c d")` would be the same as `"[a b] [a b] c d"`.
examples:
stepcat(
  sound("bd bd - cp").extend(2),
  sound("bd - sd -")
).pace(8)

functions.name: fanchor
functions.description: controls the center of the filter envelope. 0 is unipolar positive, .5 is bipolar, 1 is unipolar negative
examples:
note("{f g g c d a a#}%8").s("sawtooth").lpf("{1000}%2")
.lpenv(8).fanchor("<0 .5 1>")

functions.name: fast
functions.description: Speed up a pattern by the given factor. Used by "*" in mini notation.
examples: s("bd hh sd hh").fast(2) // s("[bd hh sd hh]*2")

functions.name: fastChunk
functions.description:
Like `chunk`, but the cycles of the source pattern aren't repeated
for each set of chunks.

functions.name: fastGap
functions.description: speeds up a pattern like fast, but rather than it playing multiple times as fast would it instead leaves a gap in the remaining space of the cycle. For example, the following will play the sound pattern "bd sn" only once but compressed into the first half of the cycle, i.e. twice as fast.

functions.name: filter
functions.description: Filters haps using the given function

functions.name: filterHaps
functions.description: Returns a new Pattern, which only returns haps that meet the given test.

params.name: hap_test
params.description: - a function which returns false for haps to be removed from the pattern

functions.name: filterValues
functions.description:
As with `filterHaps`, but the function is applied to values
inside haps.
examples:
const drums = s("bd sd bd sd")
kick: drums.filterValues((v) => v.s === 'bd').duck(2)
snare: drums.filterValues((v) => v.s === 'sd')
bass: s("saw!4").note("G#1").lpf(80).lpenv(4).orbit(2)

functions.name: filterWhen
functions.description: Filters haps by their begin time

functions.name: firstCycle
functions.description:
Queries the pattern for the first cycle, returning Haps. Mainly of use when
debugging a pattern.

params.name: with_context

functions.name: K
functions.description:
Produces a [Kabelsalat](https://kabel.salat.dev/) modular sound engine.
This can be used as either an effect (by including `audioin()` at the beginning
of your kabel expression) or as a sound source (via any expression which doesn't
start with `audioin()`).

Some helpers you have available to you:
  * Strudel mini notation works fine in K(..) via "" or ``
  * More complex Strudel expressions (like "0 1 2".fast(4) or irand(24)) can be
    written by wrapping them in `S(..)` inside your Kabel code
  * We expose Strudel's note frequency under `sFreq` and Strudel's gate
    information under `sGate`
  * You can use more complex multi-line expressions (like `let x = a; let y = b; x.lpf(y);`)
    by wrapping them inside a function in K (see example).
examples:
note("A c e".fast(4)).transpose("<0 2 4 6 8>")
  .scale("F:minor").transpose("12")
  .s("saw")
  .K(
    // audioin().mul(sGate.adsr(0.001, 0.3, 0, 0.2)) // as effect
    saw(saw(sFreq / "2!3 16").mul(8).add(sFreq).lag("0!3 0.1")).mul(0.3) // as source
    .mul(sGate.adsr(0, 0.15, 0.5, "0.1!3 1"))
    .lpf(sGate.adsr(0, 0.2, 0.3, 0.2).mul(1).add(0))
    .add(x => x.delay(S("0.3 0.2".fast(2))).mul(0.7))
    .add(x => x.delay("0.03 [0.08 0.01] 0.01 0.013").mul(0.77)).mul(0.7)
    .add(x => x.delay(.13).mul(0.7))
    .out()
  )

functions.name: scale
functions.description:
Turns numbers into notes in the scale (zero indexed) or quantizes notes to a scale.

When describing notes via numbers, note that negative numbers can be used to wrap backwards
in the scale as well as sharps or flats to produce notes outside of the scale.

Also sets scale for other scale operations, like {@link Pattern#scaleTranspose}.

A scale consists of a root note (e.g. `c4`, `c`, `f#`, `bb4`) followed by semicolon (':') and then a [scale type](https://github.com/tonaljs/tonal/blob/main/packages/scale-type/data.ts).

If your scale name includes spaces, replace them with colons.

The root note defaults to octave 3, if no octave number is given.

functions.name: transpose
functions.description:
Change the pitch of each value by the given amount. Expects numbers or note strings as values.
The amount can be given as a number of semitones or as a string in interval short notation.
If you don't care about enharmonic correctness, just use numbers. Otherwise, pass the interval of
the form: ST where S is the degree number and T the type of interval with

- M = major
- m = minor
- P = perfect
- A = augmented
- d = diminished

Examples intervals:

- 1P = unison
- 3M = major third
- 3m = minor third
- 4P = perfect fourth
- 4A = augmented fourth
- 5P = perfect fifth
- 5d = diminished fifth

params.description: Either number of semitones or interval string.

functions.name: voicing
functions.description:
Turns chord symbols into voicings. You can use the following control params:

- `chord`: Note, followed by chord symbol, e.g. C Am G7 Bb^7
- `dict`: voicing dictionary to use, falls back to default dictionary
- `anchor`: the note that is used to align the chord
- `mode`: how the voicing is aligned to the anchor
  - `below`: top note <= anchor
  - `duck`: top note <= anchor, anchor excluded
  - `above`: bottom note >= anchor
- `offset`: whole number that shifts the voicing up or down to the next voicing
- `n`: if set, the voicing is played like a scale. Overshooting numbers will be octaved

All of the above controls are optional, except `chord`.
If you pass a pattern of strings to voicing, they will be interpreted as chords.

functions.name: voicings
functions.description:
DEPRECATED: still works, but it is recommended you use .voicing instead (without s).
Turns chord symbols into voicings, using the smoothest voice leading possible.
Uses [chord-voicings package](https://github.com/felixroos/chord-voicings#chord-voicings).
examples: stack("<C^7 A7 Dm7 G7>".voicings('lefthand'), "<C3 A2 D3 G2>").note()
